chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Kathir ibn Yunus, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyaba, who said:

When my father Sayyaba died, a man from his brethren came to me and knocked on the door. I went out to him, and he offered me condolences, saying, 'Did your father leave anything?' I said to him, 'No.' So he handed me a bag containing one thousand dirhams and said, 'Keep it well and eat from its surplus.' I entered to my mother, happy, and informed her.

In the evening, I went to a friend of my father and bought Sabiriyya goods, sitting in a shop. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, granted me much goodness in it. When Hajj approached, it occurred in my heart. I went to my mother and said, 'It has occurred in my heart that I should go out to Mecca.' She said to me, 'Return the dirhams of so-and-so to him; bring them.' I brought them to him and handed them over, as if I had gifted them to him. He said, 'Perhaps you considered it small, so I will increase it for you.' I said, 'No, but Hajj has occurred in my heart, so I preferred that your money remain with you.'

Then I went out and fulfilled my Hajj rituals, then returned to Medina. I entered with the people to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who gave general permission. I sat among the back rows of the people, and I was young. People began asking him, and he answered them. When the crowd thinned, he gestured to me, so I approached him. He said to me, 'Do you have a need?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, I am Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyaba.' He said to me, 'What happened to your father?' I said, 'He died.' He expressed condolences and mercy.

He said, 'Then he said to me, 'Did he leave anything?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'From where did you perform Hajj?' I began and narrated to him the story of the man. He did not leave me until he said, 'What did you do with the one thousand?' I said, 'I returned it to its owner.' He said to me, 'You have done well.' He said to me, 'Shall I advise you?' I said, 'Yes, may I be sacrificed for you.' He said, 'Upon you is truthfulness in speech and repayment of the trust; you will share the people in their wealth like this,' and he joined his fingers together.
He said, 'So I memorized that from him, and I attained three hundred thousand dirhams.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of returning a loan and maintaining honesty in Shia ethical teachings?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the virtue of returning entrusted wealth (amanah) even when not strictly obligated, as Abd al-Rahman returned the principal after using it for trade and Hajj. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) commended his integrity and advised him to uphold truthfulness and trustworthiness, promising that these qualities would lead to significant material blessing, as evidenced by his subsequent growth of wealth to three hundred thousand dirhams.
